title: Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) Adds 5 More International Film Festivals · Reaching 13 Across 7 Countries
excerpt: Dubai, Chicago, Shivaji, Tokyo, and Italy tourism film festivals all arrived in the same month — the animated short film Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》), advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉), has accumulated 13 international nominations and official selections.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The original student animation Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) from the Department of Animation and Game Design (AGD) at Shu-Te University has once again brought great news. Following its record of 8 international film festivals in April (4) this year featured in the department's feature "Four Student Animations Sweeping International Film Festivals," the film has recently been favored by film festivals in five countries including the United Arab Emirates, the United States, India, Japan, and Italy, adding 5 nominations and selections at once, bringing its total international festival selections and nominations to 13, spanning 7 countries.

■ 5 Newly Added Selections
　• Dubai Independent Film Festival, United Arab Emirates — Best Student Short Competition · Semifinalist
　• Chicago Indie Film Awards, United States — Best Student Film Competition · Nominee
　• Chhatrapati Shivaji International Film Festival, India — Animated Short Film Competition · Official Selection
　• Tokyo International Cinema Awards, Japan — Best Animation Competition · Nominee
　• The 15th International Tour Film Festival, Italy — Animation Competition · Official Selection

■ About the Work

Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) was co-created by AGD students Chen Zhi-yang (陳志揚), Song Qiu-yang (宋秋陽), and Fujikawa Ryusei (藤川黎星), advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉). Produced entirely in 2D digital hand-drawn animation with a 1980s nostalgic art style, the film portrays the conflict between idol worship and rational cognition, exploring the boundary between "simple liking" and "complete obsession." It reminds the audience that obsession often stems from a lack of understanding, and that rational support is true growth. The work echoes SDG 4 "Quality Education" and SDG 12 "Responsible Consumption and Production," demonstrating profound critical thinking on media literacy in the social media era.

■ Domestic Achievements

"Merit Award" at the 21st Computer Animation Contest for Universities and Colleges (技專校院電腦動畫競賽) [CHECK], "Excellence Award" in the Animation Category at the 2025 Bahamut ACG Creation Contest (巴哈姆特 ACG 創作大賽) [CHECK], "Best Narrative Short Film" at the 17th Little Leopard Young Short Film Awards (小花豹青年短片大獎) [CHECK], and shortlisted in the 2D Animation Category at the 2025 Vision Get Wild (放視大賞) [CHECK].

Advising professor Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉) stated that for a student graduation project to be continuously recognized in film festivals across different countries means that the issues addressed by the work transcend language and culture. Department Chair Deng Shu-yuan (鄧樹遠) pointed out that AGD has long emphasized "practical creation × social value," encouraging students to view their graduation projects as their first portfolio entering the international market rather than the end of a course.

title: Design Power Goes Overseas! AGD Japan Internship Enters 9th Year · 4 Students Enter HC Company to Challenge Japanese Workplace
excerpt: Under the Ministry of Education's "Building Dreams Overseas" (學海築夢) program, 4 students were sent to hautecouture Inc. (HC) in Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, Japan for a nearly 3-month internship, led by Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅), extending into regional revitalization and traditional craft exchanges in Seiyo City and Tobe Town.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The international internship collaboration between the Department of Animation and Game Design (AGD) at Shu-Te University and the renowned Japanese animation and game production company hautecouture Inc. (オートクチュール株式会社, HC) has entered its 9th year. This year, both parties joined hands again to implement the Ministry of Education's "Building Dreams Overseas" (學海築夢) overseas internship program, launching an internship of nearly 3 months to substantially strengthen students' professional skills and international vision.

This project was co-planned and executed by AGD International Team members Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) and Yin Li (尹立). Based on the department's rigorous overseas internship selection mechanism, students had to pass multiple stages including training, selection, written review, preliminary tests, and Japanese interviews, as well as an all-Japanese online interview with HC. This year, a total of 4 outstanding students were admitted, including 3 students from Taiwan (Wang Yun-shu (王韻淑), Xia Yu-xin (夏妤馨), Xiao Pei-lun (蕭培綸)) and 1 student from Macau (Lai Jian-hao (賴健豪)). During the internship, they directly engaged in HC's animation and game projects, learning the industry's latest design technologies and team collaboration models.

■ From Welcome Ceremony to Project Frontlines

Project director Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) personally led the team to Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, Japan, assisting students in settling into rental housing and handling commuting cards and other living essentials to help them quickly integrate into the local community. On the 1st day of the internship, HC held a warm welcome ceremony for the students; students then attended the company morning meeting, introducing themselves in online meetings with HC executives and branch members. During the meeting, the company assigned internship tasks covering illustration design, character design, and game art painting, allowing students to enter real industry production processes and gain valuable practical experience.

■ Transnational Cultural Sharing × Regional Revitalization Experience

In addition to technical skills, this year's internship greatly deepened cultural exchanges. During the corporate internship, students actively shared the cultural characteristics of Taiwan and Macau in exchange meetings, conducting enthusiastic two-way discussions with Japanese colleagues and demonstrating youthful vitality and professional confidence in cross-border cooperation. Furthermore, Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) specifically led the internship team to Seiyo City, Ehime Prefecture, visiting the Uwa Predecessors Memorial Museum (宇和先哲記念館) and engaging in in-depth cultural dialogue with Mr. Matsumoto and Mr. Yamamoto of the Seiyo City Tourism and Local Products Association (西予市觀光物產協會) and Mr. Utsunomiya of the Economic Promotion Division of the Industry Department (產業部經濟振興課), exchanging experiences in local tourism and cultural promotion between Taiwan and Japan. The internship team also visited Tobe Town to conduct cultural filming and video documentation on its highly representative traditional craft "Tobe Ware" (砥部燒), allowing students to draw creative nourishment from fieldwork and incorporate it into design projects.

■ Previous Session's Results Landed as AR Guide

Looking back, AGD's Japan internship program has yielded fruitful results. Character designs co-produced by the previous batch of interns and local Japanese university students were successfully applied to the AR character tour event "Marutto AR Stamp Rally" (まるっとARスタンプラリー) in Tobe Town, Ehime Prefecture, Japan. The participating students' names were also publicly displayed on the official event website, receiving high praise from Japanese enterprises and local government.

Project director Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) remarked that this is not only a professional internship, but also an in-depth cross-cultural and cross-disciplinary experience, hoping students lay a solid foundation for their future careers while broadening their international perspectives. AGD Chair Deng Shu-yuan (鄧樹遠) also noted that the department has long valued students' international practical experience, and will continue to expand cooperation platforms, enabling students to step onto the world stage, unite learning with application, continually support international internship projects, and cultivate creative talents with global competitiveness.

title: AGD Graduation Project Dear, All Robots (《Dear, All Robots》) Hits International Media · Featured by CommonWealth English and Crossing
excerpt: Advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉), an Indonesian student team participated in the 2026 Youth Innovative Design Festival (青春設計節) with their graduation animated short Dear, All Robots (《Dear, All Robots》), receiving dedicated feature reports from CommonWealth English and Crossing (《換日線 Crossing》).
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The creative energy of the Department of Animation and Game Design (AGD) at Shu-Te University has once again received recognition from international media. Advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉), an Indonesian student animation team exhibited their 5-minute graduation animated short Dear, All Robots (《Dear, All Robots》) at the 2026 Youth Innovative Design Festival (青春設計節) [CHECK], recently receiving dedicated feature reports from international English media CommonWealth English and Chinese media Crossing (《換日線 Crossing》), demonstrating the department's educational outcomes in animation narrative, visual style, and cross-cultural creation.

Dear, All Robots (《Dear, All Robots》) is a short animation completed in Taiwan, depicting an office worker who gradually loses color and feels like a "robot" under work pressure and repetitive routines, but regains emotion and human warmth after a colorful one-eyed kitten enters his life. Through the contrast between black-and-white tones and vibrant colors in memory, the work reflects the shared anxiety of the young generation torn between ideals, employment, and realistic pressures.

One of the main creators, Ryan Evan Limawi, stated that many young people may not immediately find their ideal job after graduation and might lose enthusiasm in daily routine; the team hopes to convey the message that even if the 1st job does not match one's dreams, as long as one continues trying and exploring, there will still be opportunities to find a truly suitable direction in the future.

■ From Production to Exhibition Promotion

During the exhibition, in addition to screening the animated short, the team also synchronously displayed character models, posters, setting artbooks, stickers, keychains, kitten plushies, and LINE stickers, inviting audiences to write down their viewing reflections, fully demonstrating students' integrated abilities from animation production and character management to brand promotion and audience interaction.

Teacher Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉) pointed out that the most important core of animation creation includes storyboards, story content, and visual styles, and this team successfully integrated all 3 elements, demonstrating mature narrative and creative capabilities. The participating Indonesian student team also shared that Taiwan's favorable Chinese learning and animation creation environment, along with Kaohsiung's creator-friendly atmosphere, were essential forces supporting them in completing their work.

AGD expressed that the attention received by this film from international and Chinese media reflects the department's long-standing educational achievements in cross-cultural learning, capstone project production, animation narrative, character design, and integrated marketing; the department will continue cultivating animation and game design talents equipped with technical skills, humanistic care, and market communication capability.

title: Shu-Te University AGD 2026 Open Day Guides Participants to Experience the Learning Scene of Animation and Game Design
excerpt: Open Day centers on "Truly Experiencing University Learning," featuring 5 core courses + board game interaction + campus tour + group hands-on practice.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] During the winter vacation, the Department of Animation and Game Design (AGD) at Shu-Te University held the "2026 Open Day — What Do You Want @ Your University" experience event, attracting enthusiastic participation from many students and parents passionate about animation, comics, and game design.

Centering on "Truly Experiencing University Learning," the event featured 5 core courses, board game interactions, campus tours, cafe culinary exchanges, and group practical workshops, allowing participants to understand the learning features of AGD and explore their future learning directions.

This Open Day was a learning gathering blending "warmth, friendliness, and tactile experience," jointly planned by 10 professional faculty members and several senior student illustrators and designers, creating an experiential space full of care and creative energy.

Participants voted on 5 core courses for in-depth experiences, including Game Interface Design (UI/UX) (《遊戲介面設計（UI/UX）》), Comic Aesthetics (《漫畫美學》), 3D Printing Practical Applications (《3D 列印應用實務》), Animation and Game Character Merchandise Design and Production (《動畫與遊戲人物周邊設計製作》), and Animation Aesthetics Research (《動畫美學研究》). The afternoon session featured hands-on workshops grouped by participants' interests, including "Hands-on Experience in Character Merchandise Design" and "Co-creating with Senior Student Illustrators."

Department Chair Deng Shu-yuan (鄧樹遠) stated: "As AI and generative technologies rapidly enter the creative scene, although creative methods continue to evolve, the core of creation still comes from the creator's observation, feelings, and judgment."

title: Shu-Te University Achieves Great Results Again! Dual Scientific Research Stars Ranked in the World's Top 2% Scientists for 4 Consecutive Years
excerpt: Professor Su Zhong-he (蘇中和) (AGD) has been selected into the "World's Top 2% Scientists" for 4 consecutive years.
content:
According to the newly released 2025 "World's Top 2% Scientists" list, approximately 1,470 scholars in Taiwan were listed. Shu-Te University Vice President and Dean of the College of Design Professor Su Zhong-he (蘇中和) and Distinguished Professor Zhang Wei-de (張偉德) of the Department of Computer and Communication were once again both selected, earning high international recognition for their scientific research strength.

This list is a collaboration between Stanford University and Elsevier, analyzing citation data from the Scopus database to rigorously select the top 2% from nearly 800 ten-thousand (8 million) scientists worldwide.

Professor Su Zhong-he (蘇中和) holds a prominent international standing in the Social Sciences—Education field, achieving breakthrough results particularly in research on design education and gamified learning. Professor Su's research scope spans design education, gamified STEM education, digital twins, and augmented reality design, successfully branching into intelligent design and AI image processing.

President Wang Zhao-xiong (王昭雄) stated: "The international recognition of Vice President Su Zhong-he (蘇中和) and Professor Zhang Wei-de (張偉德) once again highlights Shu-Te University's educational feature of 'equal emphasis on teaching and research.'"

title: Shu-Te University AGD Wins Dual Excellence Awards at Bahamut ACG Creation Contest
excerpt: Original animations Zephyranthes (《人造人》) and Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) both won the Excellence Award, standing out among 69 shortlisted works across Taiwan.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The 2025 "ACG Creation Contest" was organized by Taiwan's largest ACG (Animation, Comics, Games) community platform, Bahamut. The Department of Animation and Game Design at Shu-Te University delivered an outstanding performance, as two original animations created by student teams, Zephyranthes (《人造人》) and Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》), both won the "Excellence Award," standing out among 69 shortlisted works across Taiwan.

Zephyranthes (《人造人》) was created by students Bo Hao-yuan (博浩原), Rong Xuan-yi (戎軒頤), Chen Zheng-min (陳政民), and Li Yu-xian (李育賢), advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉). The story explores artificial intelligent life, depicting human struggles through suspense and poetry, echoing SDG 16 "Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions."

Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) was created by students Song Qiu-yang (宋秋陽), Chen Zhi-yang (陳志揚), and Fujikawa Ryusei (藤川黎星), also advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉). Featuring a 1980s nostalgic art style to portray the conflict between idol worship and rational cognition, it incorporates SDG 4 "Quality Education" and SDG 12 "Responsible Consumption and Production."

Advising professor Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉) stated: "The students' awards in this benchmark competition demonstrate not only the maturity of their animation production techniques, but also their ability to transform life observations and social issues into deeply reflective creative outcomes."

title: Shu-Te University Partners with Major Japanese Animation Studio to Cultivate Internationally Competitive Anime and Game Design Talent
excerpt: Entering its 8th year of collaboration with Japan's hautecouture Inc. (HC), 8 students were sent under the "Building Dreams Overseas" program to Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture for a nearly 3-month internship.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The Department of Animation and Game Design (AGD) at Shu-Te University has entered its 8th year of collaboration with the well-known Japanese animation and game production company hautecouture Inc. (オートクチュール株式会社, HC). Both parties continue to deepen industry-academia cooperation, joining hands once again this year to promote the Ministry of Education's "Building Dreams Overseas" (學海築夢) program for a nearly 3-month international internship.

Co-planned and executed by AGD International Team members Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) and Yin Li (尹立), through rigorous departmental selection mechanisms, 8 outstanding students were accepted: 6 from Taiwan (Chen Si-ying (陳思穎), Huang Yu-xin (黃郁心), Chen Yu-jie (陳宇杰), Zeng Ruo-ci (曾若慈), Luo Yu-han (羅語涵), Hong Yun-han (洪韻涵)) and 2 from Malaysia (Wen Yong-sheng (溫永生), Pei Xin-hui (裴欣慧)).

Teacher Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) personally led the team to Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, Japan on July 8 (month 7, day 8), helping students settle in and familiarize themselves with the environment. Students actively participated in animation and game projects under HC, with assigned tasks covering illustration, character design, and game art.

AGD Chair Deng Shu-yuan (鄧樹遠) stated: "The department has long valued students' international practical experience, and the collaboration with HC has a solid foundation and fruitful results."

title: Shu-Te University AGD Demonstrates Creative Prowess, Winning 2nd Place in International Times Young Creative Awards
excerpt: Student work Yung-Ching Realty Employer Brand Recruitment Commercial Series (《永慶房屋雇主品牌招募廣告系列》), advised by Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅), won 2nd Place at the 34th Times Young Creative Awards.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The Department of Animation and Game Design at Shu-Te University has once again brought great news from the 34th International Times Young Creative Awards (第 34 屆時報金犢獎) [CHECK]! Advised by teacher Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅), the work Yung-Ching Realty Employer Brand Recruitment Commercial Series — Shiba Inu, Raccoon, Squirrel (《永慶房屋雇主品牌招募廣告系列篇 — 柴犬篇、浣熊篇、松鼠篇》), co-created by students Pei Xin-hui (裴欣慧), Huang Ruo-ting (黃若庭), Wang Qiao-an (王巧安), and Cai Si-qi (蔡思淇), won the 2nd place honor in the "Yung-Ching Realty Recruitment Advertising Category."

Centering on the employer brand spirit of Yung-Ching Realty, this award-winning work utilized animal character settings and vivid storytelling techniques to translate the 3 major recruitment appeals of "no contract lock-in," "no excessive overtime," and "no pay deduction" into a relaxed, humorous, and eye-catching visual language. With a parrot as the core character symbolizing corporate culture, the team launched 3 animated shorts of about 30 seconds each: Shiba Inu (《柴犬篇》) interprets flexible "no contract lock-in" career choices; Raccoon (《浣熊篇》) emphasizes the "no excessive overtime" work-life balance philosophy; Squirrel (《松鼠篇》) highlights the "no pay deduction" policy guaranteeing income.

AGD Chair Deng Shu-yuan (鄧樹遠) stated that students performed remarkably in this year's Times Young Creative Awards, not only winning 2nd place, but also seeing 18 groups of works successfully shortlisted for the finals. Among them, works advised by Zhang Chun-ya (張純雅) earned 11 shortlisted spots, and works advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉) earned 7.

The Times Young Creative Awards is acclaimed as one of the most influential youth creative competitions in the Chinese-speaking world, attracting over 10,000 entries from around the world to compete this year.

title: Shu-Te University AGD Achieves Outstanding Results in National Competitions, Led by Graduation Project The Stolen Recipe (《失竊的祕方》)
excerpt: The Stolen Recipe (《失竊的祕方》) won the Excellence Award at Youth Innovative Design Festival and was shortlisted for the National Practical Project Contest for Colleges and Universities, standing out from 1,181 entries.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] Students of the Department of Animation and Game Design at Shu-Te University performed outstandingly across multiple national design and animation competitions in 2025. Co-created by Tu Cheng-en (涂承恩), Li Guan-lin (李冠霖), Zhang Shu-ying (張淑盈), and Tang Li-rong (唐莉蓉), advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉), the 2D animated short film The Stolen Recipe (《失竊的祕方》) won multiple honors with its delicate narrative approach and deeply meaningful character portrayals.

The Stolen Recipe (《失竊的祕方》) won the Excellence Award in the "Digital Multimedia and Game Design Category / Creative Digital Video Group" at the "2025 Youth Innovative Design Festival" (2025 青春設計節) [CHECK], and was successfully shortlisted in the Anime and Interactive Multimedia category at the "2025 National Practical Project Contest for Colleges and Universities" (2025 全國技專校院學生實務專題製作競賽暨成果展) [CHECK], standing out from 1,181 registered entries nationwide.

With "misunderstanding and reconciliation" as its theme, the film depicts the story of an old chef who misunderstands a new restaurant owner due to the theft of a secret recipe book, integrating core SDGs concepts such as gender equality, reduced inequalities, and peace and justice.

In the Direct Entry Category of the 21st Computer Animation Contest for Colleges and Universities (第 21 屆技專校院電腦動畫競賽) [CHECK], AGD garnered 4 Merit Awards: Obsessive Reality (《癡迷的現實》) (advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉)), Holy Algorithm (《神癒》) (advised by Chen Qing-hong (陳慶鴻)), Zephyranthes (《人造人》) (advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉)), and The Stolen Recipe (《失竊的祕方》) (advised by Chen Mei-rong (陳美蓉)).

title: Shu-Te University AGD Week Opens Lively, 3 Major Exhibition Areas Lead into the Quest Game World
excerpt: This year's AGD Week theme "Hidden Dungeon: Open for a Limited Time" — merchandise sales, Street Fighter e-sports, student work exhibitions, and interactive quests.
content:
[Kaohsiung News] The annual "AGD Week" of the Department of Animation and Game Design at Shu-Te University kicked off under the theme "Hidden Dungeon: Open for a Limited Time" (隱藏副本限時開放中) at the Marble Plaza on the 1st floor of the College of Design.

The most attractive part of the event was the 3 major exhibition areas meticulously planned by students:
1. Animation and Game Student Merchandise Sales Booths — acrylic keychains, stickers, postcards
2. Street Fighter Esports Arena — passionate showdowns between esports players and gaming enthusiasts
3. Animation and Game Student Dynamic and Static Works Exhibition — animated shorts, character designs, game prototypes

The event also featured interactive gaming quests, where participants had to complete various challenges to receive limited exquisite gifts.

Wu Yan-sheng (吳焉昇), faculty advisor for the AGD Student Association, stated: "AGD Week is a demonstration of the results of students' hard work over the past year, handled entirely by students from preliminary planning, design, and production to on-site execution."
